title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
why_read: A robotics paper on adapting world models at test time to unknown physical properties like friction, relevant to researchers working on sim-to-real transfer.
analysis: T2-Z adds a learnable 'environment latent' to a robot's world model, letting it infer unobserved physical factors like friction or mass from just a few test-time interactions rather than requiring explicit labeling. The method shows substantial improvements in prediction error and task success across simulated and real robot tasks. This is a solid contribution to the specific technical problem of making world models adapt quickly to new environments without retraining, of interest mainly to robotics and model-based RL researchers.
